reviews.review:
[I] Her Love, Like Poison [/i] was an emotional read, mostly in a negative way though but it felt not that bad really. It's way better than indifference anyway. And I honestly don't mind when smth can evoke powerful emotions within me. Though I felt a tad poisoned myself with all that anger, annoyance and hatred I was forced to experience :)
SPOILERS ahead...
The story is short but atmospheric and as usual well-written. The main character was so unbearable I'd have quit quite soon if not a superb ebi-hime's writing. For me it was the most enjoyable part.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3600930477 
So, about the protagonist (－‸ლ) I really tried hard to sympathize with her. I guess she has a number of traits that can make her relatable at first glance, like no energy to write her thesis, pain from the breakup, feeling that no one understands you etc... But soon enough all her incessant ramblings becomes infuriating. 

She keeps repeating her age again and again in different situations as if trying to persuade herself and me, as a reader, what an adult she already is at the age of 21 O_o But nope, her behavior and way of thinking is still way too immature, selfish AND stupid. Especially disgusting was the moment when she lied AGAIN to a sincerely caring person and after a fleeting twinge of guilt justified her deceit with the fact that she doesn't owe him anything O_o That's it! We have to be indebted to behave like a decent person(－‸ლ) I'll always choose a blunt, frank and even rude person to a lying, pretending hypocrite.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3601865042
She doesn't seem to appreciate at all how lucky she is to have nice, loving parents, yeah, right, they are too different, they don't share or understand her interests and they may be not always considerate but isn't it this way all the time for all families due to that inevitable generation gap?! They still try their best to provide her with everything she needs like paying for her violin lessons and spending lots of time driving her to the private teacher. Is mc even grateful for that? Accepting her tragic fate without any fight at all at the end of the story, enjoying her delusional 'happiness' does she ever spare at least a fleeting thought to her family who must be still grieving her or even keep searching for her in the woods?! Or what about her teacher who tried to warn her and talk against going into the forest at night. Has she ever thought about all his efforts?! Nope! Never! She's too self-centered, she's the only one she cares about. I'm all for healthy egoism myself. But after all her constant complaints that others don't care about her enough … It IS hypocritical to demand smth from others that you can't do yourself and she called herself an adult(－‸ლ) Welp, because of her revolting attitude I also stopped caring quite soon.
And finally about her ex-girlfriend... That poor, patient girl must have really loved her to tolerate that infuriatingly deprecating attitude for the whole year... I know how it feels to deal with wet blankets and naysayers. If a person sees only negativity, no reassuring and encouraging can fix anything. Their wild imagination is too powerful in this regard making up countless excuses why they don't deserve to be happy and are doomed to fail. Such people need professional help. She can't be excused as someone suffering from depression because of that breakup, her issues are more serious and she had to deal with them way before that split-up.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3603897095 
Unfortunately, I spoiled myself that plot twist at the store page:( But though it wasn't surprising anymore I still found that part enjoyable. I was always fascinated with mushrooms. My mum likes to pick them and we lived near the forest, too. I was never good at that myself but I love eating them. Though as a vegan I question myself occasionally if it's actually right. Mushrooms are such curious creatures, even classified into a separate kingdom by scientists as they have features of both plants and animals. The way that collective existing works is truly amazing. So remembering all that it was exciting to read the final parts, though again I was annoyed how weak mc was. I even wished it wasn't a linear novel and I could influence anything. Starting from the very first decision to go to Australia with family, lol, and at the very end to fight for maybe miserable but real existence.

Welp, despite lots of intense negative emotions it was a pleasant read. Such depressing things inspire me to be more proactive if mc couldn't. And btw it WAS depressing indeed to read how life isn't valued at all, how sick, infected mind prefers to be devoured for the sake of the illusion of being needed... When I'm shown so vividly how wrong someone's choices and world perception are I feel motivated to choose the opposite :D
